headline: RegalCare agrees to $1 million settlement over nursing-home billing allegations
dek: The Massachusetts operator and two executives agreed to resolve allegations that they billed Medicare and MassHealth for medically unnecessary skilled-rehabilitation services.
body: A nursing-home operator with facilities in Massachusetts and two executives have agreed to pay $1 million to resolve allegations that they submitted claims to Medicare and MassHealth for medically unnecessary skilled-rehabilitation services, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for Massachusetts said Wednesday.

The settlement covers RegalCare Management Group, RegalCare Management 2.0, owner Eliyahu Mirlis and executive Hector Caraballo. Federal prosecutors said the companies operated skilled-nursing facilities in Massachusetts and previously in Connecticut, and that the government and Massachusetts filed a civil False Claims Act complaint in 2025.

The allegations covered claims made from 2018 through 2023. According to the Justice Department, RegalCare submitted claims that were not supported by individual patient need, while records were modified to support higher-paying Medicare categories. The parties admitted those facts as part of the settlement agreement.

The case began with a whistleblower lawsuit filed under the False Claims Act’s qui tam provisions. The relator will receive $165,000 from the recovery, prosecutors said. A related settlement with RegalCare’s therapy provider, Stern Therapy, was announced in March and addressed allegations tied to unnecessary rehabilitation claims.

Massachusetts Attorney General Andrea Joy Campbell and U.S. Attorney Leah Foley announced the agreement jointly with federal health-care investigators. The payment resolves the civil allegations described in the government’s complaint while preserving the case’s focus on the accuracy of billing to public health programs.
